entries.title: Switch ships and pick pilots from anywhere
items: The Ships tab in the Parts hold now shows every ship you own with a picture and its numbers, and works anywhere: out in space or at any station.
Fly this one: switch to any of your ships on the spot (not in the middle of a fight). Your crew comes with you, and if a mercenary was flying it they take over your old ship.
Choose pilot: give any hired mercenary a ship, move them between ships, or swap one pilot for another. Each pilot shows whether they can handle the ship, and why not if they can't.

entries.title: Asteroids keep their look while you mine
items: Mining or shooting a block out of an asteroid no longer reshuffles the rock texture on the rest of it. Every block keeps the same look until it breaks, and pieces that break off keep theirs too.

entries.title: Missile defence and five kinds of missile
items: Big ships no longer bury you in missiles. A bug made some launchers fire their whole volley over and over (one swarm pod sent 57 missiles instead of 8). Enemies now carry a few launchers each, reload slower, and show a red ring and a lock tone before they fire. Smaller enemy ships fight smarter and hit a little harder instead.
Rocket pods now fire the 4 rockets their card always promised (the same bug gave them extra).

Missile defence for small ships: the Blast Screen (a shield bubble that shrugs off explosions and missiles) and the Decoy Launcher (throws flares that pull chasing missiles away). Every outfitter stocks both, plus a flak or point-defence gun. Shields now flash when they stop a missile.

Five kinds of missile: Ram torpedoes (very fast, punch through a block), Blastcap (huge blast), Homing, Ion (wrecks shields, briefly jams guns and engines) and Firebrand (sets blocks burning). Ion and Firebrand are rare near home.

Your bridge now sets how many CPU and power parts can run. Bridge Mk II and Mk III (1x1) raise the limits — see the new Bridge shelf at outfitters. CPU nodes are a longer goal now: +2 CPU, 1,200 cr. Parts over the limit stay fitted but sit idle.
Build mode and Ship upgrades now spell out the road to bigger parts: 2x2 parts need a Frigate (Grow hull at a shipyard: Skiff, then Corvette, then Frigate).
Drones look like tiny ships now, keep up when you boost or cruise, and you choose which ones fly in the hold's Drones tab. Mining drones are much faster and better ones mine more.
Crafting and sealed caches spin a rarity reel weighted by the real odds. Tap to skip.

Jobs show where to go: an arrow at the screen edge with the distance, and a marker on the radar and local map that sits on top. A tow job points at the ship, then at where it goes, and the station pulls it in with a tractor beam.

Buying at the salvage yard shows exactly what you got and where it went. Asteroid scans only name an ore when there is real ore inside. Rich ore fields are just rich rocks to mine — no more claims. Insurance is at every station.
Phone: hold your thumb where you want to shoot; missiles fire by themselves.
Keys: I opens the cargo hold; C, I, N, M and J close their panel when pressed again. Boost stays off when it runs dry until it refills to 30%.
Fixed: planets that drew the wrong surface or a second smaller copy after a jump.

entries.title: Expansion: Shipwright
items: Grow your ship: refit your own hull into the next class at any shipyard, keeping every block. Pay in credits, or in ore you mined yourself.

Crafting: every station has a Workshop where you turn ore into parts and drones. Add rare ore for better odds of a fine roll, re-roll one bonus on a part, and open sealed caches (always rare or better inside). A Fabricator part lets you craft out in space.

Simpler ore: each region has just Rock plus one structural, one energy and one rare ore. Asteroids now hold one kind of ore, with the odd mixed one. Press Scan (V) to find what is around you; a Scanner part reaches much further.

Rare loot that matters: a legendary part is now far stronger than a rare one, every kind of part can roll bonuses (CPU, crew room and cargo too), and epic or better finds get a big reveal with a comparison to what you have fitted. Twenty named uniques wait in special places — check the collection log in the parts hold.

Fire every gun yourself. A gun aims and fires on its own only when it holds a targeting slot (your bridge gives two; Targeting computers add more). Sentry guns and point defence always look after themselves.
Crew is just a number now: '+3 Crew'. Each ship shows the least crew it needs to fly, what it needs for full strength, and how many fit. Hire more or sell the extra at a crew hall.
Drones are their own items: buy, craft or find them, then fit them to drone ports in build mode. A lost drone is rebuilt for free after a few seconds. Mender drones patch your wingmen too.
Mercenaries: hire a pilot and give them a ship from your hangar. They fly beside you and fight for you. Better pilots wait at more dangerous stations.

Your own outposts: fly over a planet and found an outpost. Build ore sites, a research lab, a factory, a trade post and defence turrets — they keep working while you are away. Raiders sometimes come, with a warning.
Missions at station and outpost boards: tow things back with your harpoon, deliveries, clear a site, escort a freighter, survey asteroids, or find something they need.

More to run into: convoys under attack, wandering merchants, space rifts, ion clouds, comets, derelict stations, wanted captains, ambushes, small friendly outposts, corsair vaults, alien nests and abandoned outposts to search.
Galaxy events: alien invasions, gold rushes, pirate wars and treasure systems sweep across the star map for a while.
The outfitter is sorted by slot, the star map lists what each station offers, and a new Ship upgrades screen (menu) shows what to improve next.

Looks: brand-new planets with real lighting, air, clouds and city lights; stronger weapons glow brighter and beams spiral; much bigger boost flames with sound; rare drops light up a pillar you can see from afar.
Smoother: no more flicker or blur when flying fast. Ship and asteroid edges are clean, with no stray squares or backward corners.

Fixes: the title logo fits every screen; gnats no longer limp on as a single block; boost gives a real kick; undocking puts you back on the side you came in from; all features open after the 'Further out' goal, and the old harpoon goal is gone.

entries.title: Fairer enemies, and gnat packs
items: Enemies are back to their old toughness: the extra hull from the last update is gone and your missiles hit them with full force again. They still keep the slower guns, and bases still carry fewer guns.

Gnats: new tiny enemy fighters with one small gun and no shields. They fly in packs of five to nine and go down fast, so a pack is a fun fight for any ship. Look for gnat packs (orange) on the local map.

entries.title: Bigger systems, real fights, a local map
items: Star systems are now huge. Asteroid clusters, enemy camps, alien swarms, wreck fields and trade convoys fill the space between planets as you fly, so there is always something nearby.
Cruise: when no enemy is close and you are out of combat, your engines open up so you can cross a system quickly.
New local map (N, or tap the radar): the whole system with stations, planets, asteroid clusters, enemy camps, ships and points of interest, with a key. Tap anything to set a course marker.
About three times as many enemies, and they are tougher: more hull, slower guns, and a missile blast can no longer erase a whole ship in one go. Fights last long enough for both sides to fight.
Every star is different: busier or quieter enemies, better or ordinary finds, more or fewer asteroids, its size and its economy. The star map shows it all.

Warp cores: your core decides how dangerous a star you can jump into (Class I reaches danger 2). Buy upgrades at any outfitter with credits and materials. Locked stars show a padlock; safer stars are always in reach.
Enemy bases carry a few big guns instead of a ring of them, and fire more slowly.
Safe launch: after you undock or arrive, you get a few seconds where nothing can hurt you, and enemies are moved off the station's doorstep. No more dying the moment you leave a station.

No friendly fire: your shots pass through allies, bumping into allies does nothing, and allies now steer around you. Only real fights with enemies count as combat, so building is no longer blocked by mistake. An "In combat" tag shows when you are.
Your guns never fire at friendly stations any more, and stations never turn on you over your standing. If an old fight had soured your standing with the traders or the navy, it is reset.
Power is shown and judged in whole numbers: 10 made and 10 used is enough.

entries.title: No more message pile-ups
items: A full cargo hold now warns you once instead of stacking the same message down the screen for every rock you fly past.
The same message never shows twice at once anywhere in the game — a repeat just keeps the one already on screen.

entries.title: Star map fix
items: The star map now opens when you finish "Make it yours", so you can actually do "Further out" — before, the map stayed locked behind the very goal that asked you to use it. If you were stuck there, it is open now.
Drone shops open after "Buy low, sell high", ready for the drone goal that follows.

entries.title: Phone fixes
items: The Dock button works on iPhone again.
The "Dock at …" sign is a button too — tap it to dock.
Tap the Cargo / CPU / Crew numbers under your health bar to open your hold on the Cargo tab. The menu entry is now called "Parts hold, cargo & drones".

entries.title: Fixes and louder lasers
items: Laser turrets now sound like lasers — a sharp crack and a punchy zap instead of a thin beep. Heavy lasers got a deeper voice too, and laser hits land harder.
The parts hold no longer shows a line of garbled text after you switch tabs; parts show full cards with their numbers.
Part bonuses that did nothing now work: Tuned engines push harder, Efficient parts draw less power, Nimble gyros turn faster, and Overdrive engines boost faster and longer.
Friendly ships' shots no longer hit you.
Chunks blown off a ship keep their armour instead of falling apart at the first touch.
Letting go of a harpooned wreck lets it drift off and vanish like other wreckage.
The "Repairs need ferrite" warning goes away once you have ferrite again.
Ore scooped into a nearly full hold now counts toward your mining goal.
Rescued crew start helping your ship right away.
Enemy ships no longer pick fights with asteroids they bump into.
Erasing a destroyed stock part in Build mode no longer gives you a free new one.
Buying a good and selling it straight back no longer makes money.

entries.title: First flight
items: Build your ship from square blocks — hull, armour, guns, shields, engines, reactors, drone bays — and watch the hull smooth itself into slopes.
Over 40 weapons: laser turrets, gatlings, homing missiles, dumb-fire rockets, aimed beams, railguns, plasma, lightning that leaps between ships, flak, mines, capital guns.
Mine asteroids cell by cell, or hover low over a planet and cut ore from the ground.
Trade between stations: prices follow supply and demand, events shake them up, and the market shows where each thing sells best.
Harpoon rocks and ships and drag them around. Drones fly ahead of you into the fight.
Seven factions including four alien races, a galaxy of 46 stars that gets more dangerous the further in you go, roaming giants, derelicts, distress calls and strongholds.
A goal line that opens the game up one piece at a time — and parts you find can unlock things early.
